culture.title: Code-switching is normal
culture.note: Mixing Hindi and English mid-sentence is how urban India actually talks; full textbook Hindi sounds formal.

culture.title: Yaar
culture.note: 'Mate' or 'dude', and it softens almost anything.

nonverbal.norms: In Mumbai and Delhi, friendly eye contact with natural glances away is normal; the side-to-side head wobble means 'yes, go on, I'm with you', not 'no'.

fillers.tip: When you need a second to think, say «matlab…» or «woh…» instead of «um».

tips.other: «Tu» sounds very intimate, or rude, with someone you just met; use «tum» or «aap».

cultural_moments.milestone: The family question: talk about your family, or ask about theirs, or match their banter
cultural_moments.evidence: The learner, in Hindi or Hinglish, answers the date's question about family: says something about their own family or asks about the date's.
cultural_moments.cue: Ask, warmly and a little cheekily, about their family: who they live with, and whether their parents keep asking when they will settle down. One short line.
